lines: What makes the app different?
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

lines: Separate sessions: run focused tasks in parallel, each in its own worktree.
See the work: keep plans, diffs, terminal output, and browser preview in one session.

Share state: use a canvas to keep decisions and validation evidence visible beside the work.

lines: GitHub + Copilot: from code to collaboration
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

rows.text: Shared repositories, issues, branches, pull requests, and reviews.
Understand code, explore options, draft changes, and create tests.
Take defined tasks; people direct, review, and decide what ships.
Reduce repetitive work while staying accountable for quality.

lines: What is the GitHub Copilot app?
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

lines: A desktop workspace for working with Copilot agents across software tasks—not just
another chat window.
Each session keeps a task's conversation and work together; worktrees can isolate changes.
See and manage work in context: plans, file changes, terminal, browser preview, and
canvases.
Coordinate multiple tasks, then inspect the evidence and decide what is ready to share.
Skills and agents: guidance meets a focused role
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

lines: A skill packages reusable instructions and resources for a task that comes up repeatedly.
Example: book-app-reviewer gives Copilot a consistent checklist for filters, stats, and
accessibility.
A custom agent is a named role with focused instructions and selected tools—not a newly
trained model.
Example: Book App Reviewer is read-only; it reports findings, while a person decides what to
change and verifies the result.
The GitHub work loop
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

rows.text: State the need and what success looks like.

lines: 90 minutes · the learning path
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

lines: 0–6 · Orient: what the app adds beyond a single chat.
6–15 · Explore the Book App and define a small user need.
15–25 · Instructor demo: sessions, worktrees, and reviewing a plan.
25–45 · Hands-on: plan and implement Clear filters in an isolated session.
45–68 · See a reviewer agent find an edge case; create and test your own agent.
68–74 · Instructor demo: connect an external tool with WorkIQ MCP.
74–85 · Prove the work: inspect the diff, run checks, and test in Browser.
85–90 · Debrief and choose a three-day experiment.

lines: Agent example · a role with boundaries
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

lines: The Book App Reviewer is a repository-defined custom agent: a focused role, instructions,
and selected tools.
It is not a new model; its read-only tools let it inspect and report without editing the app.
Run it against the Clear filters implementation and show its whitespace-only search finding.
The reviewer identifies a concern; the coding agent makes the fix, and people verify the
outcome.
Choose a focused job for your agent
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

lines: Code reviewer: find behavior gaps and cite code evidence; read-only.
Test designer: suggest edge cases, or write focused tests when allowed.
Bug investigator: trace a symptom to likely causes; show evidence.
Accessibility helper: audit labels and keyboard use, or make an approved fix.
Code explainer: teach where a feature or behavior lives; read-only.
Feature builder: implement one small change after a plan; inspect the diff.
Documentation helper: draft or update one named document.

lines: Mini-teach · Keep the work in context
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

rows.text: Why it matters in the app
Describe this task and the outcome you need now.
Ground work in the project files and existing patterns.
Keep task history visible and changes isolated.
Track status, then verify with the diff, tests, and browser.

lines: Instructor demo · WorkIQ through MCP
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

lines: MCP connects an agent session to tools and information beyond the repository.
Watch the facilitator use a preconfigured WorkIQ server for one safe, authorized example.
Notice when the agent calls the tool, what information it receives, and how the result helps
the task.
Participants observe only; no WorkIQ setup or account access is required.
Treat tool output as context to review, not as proof that code or a decision is correct.
Mini-teach · Canvas as the shared board
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

lines: Create or open a compact work board in the session side panel.
Track the feature plan, implementation, chosen agent role and work, and verification
evidence.
The canvas makes status visible; it does not replace reviewing the diff or running checks.
Use the board to tell what needs attention without searching a long chat.

lines: Compare the evidence
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

lines: Build session · What files changed? Does the diff match the plan? Did tests and build pass?
Custom agent · Did it do the selected job? Is its output grounded in evidence?
Browser · What behavior did you personally observe?
Canvas · Does the board reflect actual status, including anything not run?
Takeaways
cmds.name: QA:slide_title

lines: The app is a place to coordinate work, not only ask for code.
Separate sessions make concurrent tasks visible and isolated.
Skills and custom agents shape how help is delivered; MCP adds tools and information.
A canvas keeps status visible; people still inspect diffs and evidence.
Use the next three days to experiment with the app and workshop repository.
